title: A row-invariant prompt GEMM in Triton: 16-bit x [M][K] times dense [N][K] on tensor cores in fixed tiles with one K loop, whatever M is

mm.what: a BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N tile a program (grouped by GROUP_M 8), FP32 accumulation of tl.dot over one K loop of BLOCK_K steps, no split of K; MM_SMALL's 64 x 64 tile where the knobs' tile would not fill the device twice over (SMALL); at 1 to 32 rows untuned a 16 x 64 tile (4 warps, 6 stages, no switch): the same K loop, so the same bits

BLOCK_K.what: the K loop's step (each output's sum runs over K in these steps)

STAGES.what: num_stages: K steps of loads in flight

SMALL.what: take MM_SMALL's 64 x 64 tile (4 warps, 4 stages, the knobs' BLOCK_K) where the knobs' tile would not fill the device twice over

yardstick.library: cuBLAS (torch.matmul) on the same BF16 operands, its heuristic's kernel at each row count

mm-split.what: mm with K split over SPLIT programs a tile (each K range in BLOCK_K steps), the FP32 partials added in split order by a second pass and rounded once: more programs for narrow matrices at a few rows; NOT row invariant (the split, and so a row's sums, may follow the row count); deterministic

STAGES.what: num_stages: K steps of loads in flight

SPLIT.what: programs K is split over (0: as many, up to 4 and at least 1,024 values of K each, as bring the tiles to the device's multiprocessors)

yardstick.library: cuBLAS (torch.matmul) on the same BF16 operands, its heuristic's kernel (split-K included) at each row count

cuda-mm.what: the CUDA GEMM (cuda_gemm.cu, kernel.json "cuda"): a CTA TM rows x TN columns, a STAGES-deep cp.async ring of swizzled BK-byte tiles (kernel core tile.cuh), m16n8k16 BF16 / FP16 MMAs from ldmatrix fragments read a k-step ahead, persistent CTAs in a grouped order, the FP32 sums rounded once in the epilogue (gemm_epilogue.cuh); every output summed over K in k16 steps in increasing order into one accumulator whatever the knobs and the row count: row invariant, one configuration a shape for every row count

TN.what: output columns (weight rows) a CTA computes

WM.what: warps along the rows (a warp TM / WM rows)

WN.what: warps along the columns (a warp TN / WN columns)

BK.what: bytes of every row a stage (32 or 64 values of K)

STAGES.what: stages of the cp.async ring (STAGES - 1 in flight)

GROUP.what: column tiles a group of the CTA order (the CTAs that run together share their weight rows)

EPI.what: epilogue: 0 stores from registers while the CTA's next tile loads, 1 staged through shared memory as whole rows

yardstick.library: cuBLAS (torch.matmul) on the same BF16 operands, its heuristic's kernel at each row count

cuda-mm-split.what: cuda-mm with K split over SPLIT CTAs a tile (each K range in BK steps), the FP32 partials added in split order by a second pass and rounded once: more CTAs for narrow matrices at a few rows; NOT row invariant (the split may follow the row count); deterministic

TN.what: output columns (weight rows) a CTA computes

WM.what: warps along the rows (a warp TM / WM rows)

WN.what: warps along the columns (a warp TN / WN columns)

BK.what: bytes of every row a stage (32 or 64 values of K)

STAGES.what: stages of the cp.async ring (STAGES - 1 in flight)

GROUP.what: column tiles a group of the CTA order (the CTAs that run together share their weight rows)

EPI.what: epilogue: 0 stores from registers while the CTA's next tile loads, 1 staged through shared memory as whole rows

SPLIT.what: CTAs K is split over a tile (0: as many, up to 4 and at least 1,024 values of K each, as bring the tiles to the device's multiprocessors)

yardstick.library: cuBLAS (torch.matmul) on the same BF16 operands, its heuristic's kernel (split-K included) at each row count
